cohort: A 32-year-old female with obesity and hidradenitis suppurativa who underwent an uncomplicated cesarean section.
finding: A 32-year-old female died from necrotizing wound infection and septic shock caused by Streptococcus pyogenes, four days after an uncomplicated cesarean section, potentially exacerbated by pre-existing hidradenitis suppurativa.
mod_finding: The case highlights the potential for necrotizing wound infections as lethal complications of surgeries, including cesarean deliveries, and the resurgence of Group A Streptococcus (GAS) as a cause of puerperal sepsis-associated deaths.
